A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LBM work. All 25 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LBM experiments on object removal, depth and normal estimation, relighting, shadow generation, and restoration, including quantitative results and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds object-removal training controls and measurements of computational resource use.

M1.justification: The latent bridge formulation, drift and pixel losses, conditioning, timestep sampling, and proposed architecture remain unchanged. Figure 2 clarifies concatenation already described in v1; the added training controls do not revise the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Dataset and task coverage is retained, including both coarse and fine RORD masks and the appendix restoration examples. The new controls reuse existing data and resolution coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds DepthFM to the depth comparison in Table 7, previously Table 6, and introduces a pixel-space bridge comparator in Table 8. The object-removal competitors remain LAMA, SDXL-Inpainting, PowerPaint, and Attentive Eraser.

E3.justification: Appendix B introduces RORD-only fine-tuning with approximately 400k samples seen per trainable model and a separate RORD-only scratch control. Tables 6 and 8 add resource-measurement protocols over 50 and 10 images, respectively, including comparisons at resolutions 256 and 1024. These substantially extend the evaluation controls. Table 5 also gains a fine-tuning caption despite retaining its old numbers, leaving their setting ambiguous.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial analyses of training-data effects and computational scaling: shared RORD fine-tuning and a RORD-only scratch control in Appendix B, plus pixel-versus-latent training and inference costs in Appendix E. The existing parameter ablations, synthetic-data analysis, and failure cases remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new averages over 50 and 10 images specify resource-benchmark sample sizes, without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial result sets for fine-tuning, scratch training, and resource profiling. Table 6 reports fine-tuned LBM coarse/fine FID of 26.9/15.7; Table 8 reports 1024-resolution inference latency of 20.11 seconds for the pixel model versus 0.27 seconds for the latent model. These are new experimental comparisons. Adding DepthFM changes LBM's depth average rank from 3.5 to 3.7, while retained per-dataset scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1-7 and the mathematical treatment of bridge matching, latent interpolation, and training objectives are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of scalable single-step image translation, competitive performance across tasks, conditional generation, and benefits from stochasticity. The appendix additions support these existing scientific claims.

C2.justification: Appendix E extends the general dimensionality-reduction rationale by explicitly linking measured memory savings to eightfold VAE compression and keeping the VAE frozen. Existing interpretations of stochasticity, timestep sampling, failure cases, and the paired-data limitation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds the VAE compression factor, approximately 18 hours of initial LBM training on two H100 GPUs, and hardware and measurement details for the new resource benchmarks. Appendix A's existing settings remain unchanged. The abstract drops 'open-source' while retaining the implementation link; an actual availability or licensing change cannot be established.

R1.justification: The same 121 references and research positioning are retained. DepthFM was already cited in v1, and Appendix E reuses the existing latent-diffusion reference and motivation. Bibliographic differences concern citation-page backreferences.

P1.justification: Most prose remains verbatim. Changes comprise limited abstract wording, heading capitalization, localized appendix additions, and insertion of the resource-analysis section, which renames the former Appendix E as Appendix F.

P2.justification: v2 enlarges and redraws Figure 2 with a concatenation label, adds Tables 6 and 8, and extends and renumbers the depth table. Table 5 and failure-case figures move within the appendices, and front-page text reflows. The original qualitative examples remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The RORD fine-tuning and scratch controls strengthen comparison credibility, while the resource measurements provide direct evidence for the latent design's efficiency. These targeted gains outweigh a reporting ambiguity: Table 5 retains v1's numbers but now describes them as fine-tuned, alongside separate fine-tuning results in Table 6. The core method and most existing evidence remain unchanged.
